The business case in plain language

The prototype is working today. The next step is a controlled hotel pilot using approved Amex data and owners.

Product

What It Does

Confirms what the Member means, chooses the best valid option, and checks the real result after purchase.

Opportunity

What Is Missing Today

Payment systems can prove permission. They do not always prove that the final choice matched the Member’s practical goal.

Enterprise value

Why Amex Benefits

More visible Membership value, fewer avoidable wrong outcomes, and a ready-made evidence package for servicing.

Estimated effort

Medium for a Shadow Pilot

Planning estimate: 8 to 12 weeks after data access and owner approval. Production expansion is a separate, higher-effort phase.

MembersFewer questions and clearer control
MembershipValue used only when eligibility is proven
ServicingLess time rebuilding what happened
Merchants & ETSOne outcome format across channels

After the purchase

Check what actually happened

A separate checker compares the approved details with order and payment updates. The buying agent cannot change the result.

Why separate?The system that made the choice should not grade its own work.
Event translator Technical name: protocol adapter. It turns updates from AP2, UCP, or ACP into the same simple event format.

What Happened These are order, payment, and benefit updates translated into one consistent list.

Read only

Approve the details above to turn on checking.

Result and proof Technical name: Living Trust Receipt. Each fact can be matched, waiting, inferred, missing, or changed.

Fits beside ACE

It does not replace payment infrastructure

ACE and commerce protocols help establish identity, permission, credentials, and transaction facts. Outcome Assurance uses those facts to check the result.

Existing systems answer

Can this agent make this payment?

Identity, permission, credentials, checkout, order, and payment facts.

+
Outcome Assurance answers

Did the Member get the approved result?

Clear requirements, best valid choice, Membership value, proof, and support handoff.

Use approved inputs, not invented savings

Every input is editable. Defaults show how the model works and are not Amex forecasts.

Illustrative only
Modeled gross valueNot calculated
Modeled net valueNot calculated
Break-even value liftNot calculated

Gross value = avoided recovery cost + verified Membership value. Net value = gross value - operating cost. Conversion and brand effects stay out until measured.

Does the same logic work beyond one demo?

Research behind the problemWhy clear meaning and independent proof matter
Decision stability

Context can change an agent’s choice

Wharton tested roughly 26,000 shopping runs and found that ordering, memory, and retrieval format could change selections.

Wharton Generative AI Labs
Customer trust

Travelers still want trusted booking support

Expedia’s 2026 survey found that 66% would not trust an AI assistant to book on their behalf.

Expedia Group
Competitor pattern

Shopping assistants remember preferences

Amazon’s assistant uses shopping history and conversational context for recommendations. Outcome Assurance focuses on explicit approval and proof after purchase.

Amazon
Security

Merchant text can try to redirect an agent

Structured, approved fields stay separate from untrusted merchant language in this prototype.

Palo Alto Networks Unit 42
